findings.explanation: getUri treats its argument as a configuration object; the assumed string URL is config.url, not request's separate string-URL shorthand. In order, it replaces config with mergeConfig(this.defaults, config), passes exactly the merged baseURL, url, and allowAbsoluteUrls to buildFullPath, then passes that fullPath plus the merged params and paramsSerializer to buildURL. On success it synchronously returns buildURL's URI string. There is no Promise, catch, or dispatch in this method, so serializer/encoder errors and other helper exceptions propagate synchronously. It does not enter request/_request, run request interceptors, invoke an adapter, or dispatch network I/O.

mergeConfig constructs a fresh top-level result from the own enumerable keys of the defaults and per-call objects. Its merge machinery writes into new plain objects and copies arrays, so it does not assign into ordinary source configurations. url has the per-call-only rule: a non-undefined per-call value is selected, while an absent or explicitly undefined value does not inherit defaults.url. baseURL and paramsSerializer use defaultToConfig2: absent/undefined inherits the instance value, whereas any defined value wins, including null; therefore null disables an inherited base or serializer, and an empty-string base also overrides an inherited base. A per-call paramsSerializer object replaces rather than combines with the default serializer object, although the selected plain object is cloned.

params and allowAbsoluteUrls are absent from the special map and therefore use mergeDeepProperties. A defined per-call null or false wins; undefined inherits. When both sides are plain objects, utils.merge recursively combines them and later values take precedence. A selected plain object is recursively copied; an encountered array is replaced with a shallow slice rather than concatenated. The returned config is consequently not a universal deep clone: non-plain values such as native URLSearchParams and Dates are retained by reference, and array elements can also remain shared.

isAbsoluteURL recognizes, case-insensitively, strings beginning with either scheme://, where the scheme starts with a letter and then contains letters, digits, plus, period, or hyphen, or with // for a protocol-relative URL. Other strings, including /path and schemes without //, are treated as relative.

A truthy nonempty baseURL is combined with every relative URL. An absolute or protocol-relative URL is combined only when allowAbsoluteUrls is explicitly false; true or absence leaves it unchanged. getUri does not perform request's separate defaulting of an absent flag to true, but absence has the same path-selection effect because only false forces combination. A merged null, empty-string, or absent base is falsy, so the requested URL remains unchanged even when allowAbsoluteUrls is false.

combineURLs is textual: for a nonempty requested URL it removes the final one or two slashes matched at the end of the base, inserts one slash, and removes all leading slashes from the requested string. Thus forced combination of //host/path strips that leading //, while scheme://host remains embedded after the inserted slash. If the requested string is empty, it returns the base exactly. This is not URL resolution: it does not enforce an origin, interpret components, or normalize dot-segment traversal.

Absent, undefined, or null params take the immediate fast path and leave the full path unchanged. An empty plain object is truthy, so it reaches serialization but normally produces an empty string and still leaves the path unchanged.

A function-form paramsSerializer is normalized to a new object whose serialize property is that function; it is then called as serialize(params, normalizedOptions). Object form is not normalized, and its serialize callback receives params and that merged options object. A serialize callback has first precedence regardless of whether params is native URLSearchParams or a plain object, and its returned string is used verbatim. Without serialize, native URLSearchParams delegates directly to its own toString(); otherwise AxiosURLSearchParams performs plain-object processing.

An options.encode callback is selected before normalization but is used only by the plain-object AxiosURLSearchParams.toString path when serialize is absent. It is called for every materialized key and value, with the value and AxiosURLSearchParams' internal encoder as arguments. Native URLSearchParams and custom serialize bypass it. Exceptions from serialize or encode are not caught and escape getUri synchronously.

Only a nonempty serialized string triggers URL modification. At that point the first # and everything after it are removed; the fragment remains intact when serialization yields an empty string. The code then examines the fragment-free URL and appends ? if it contains no question mark, otherwise &, followed by the serialized string.

For the default plain-object path, AxiosURLSearchParams creates an empty _pairs accumulator and passes itself to toFormData as the append target. toFormData's default visitor traverses plain objects and arrays; each append stores a [key, value] pair, after which AxiosURLSearchParams encodes both sides as key=value and joins pairs with &.

Undefined and null object members are filtered before visiting, and null/undefined flat-array elements are likewise skipped. A flat array means one containing no nested plain object or array. For a root object's flat-array property, default indexes:false emits the repeated key name[] for each retained element. The flat-array shortcut is guarded by !path: a flat array nested below another object is instead recursively visited and uses explicit numeric path components, such as outer[arr][0]. Nested plain-object members use bracket paths such as outer[inner].

Dates become toISOString() strings and booleans become true or false strings; other ordinary scalars flow to encoding. Although convertValue has a null-to-empty-string case, ordinary null members in this traversal are omitted before it is called. With the URI builder's default encoder, spaces become +, colon, dollar, and comma are restored to literal characters after encodeURIComponent, while generated brackets remain percent encoded as %5B and %5D. Native URLSearchParams bypasses this accumulator, visitor, and encoder and uses its own toString(); a custom serialize callback bypasses the entire materialization path, while an encode-only option changes encoding after the same default pair materialization.
